profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the engineering lead building the study platform and the research operations manager coordinating session logistics for an internal software-engineering study on how individual thinking time affects introverts' participation in architecture discussions. The study will run next week across multiple 4-person engineer teams in two conditions: control teams go straight into a collaborative architecture meeting, while treatment teams first get solo work time and then meet. The meeting context is that recruiting is nearly complete, the facilitation guide has been drafted, and both workstreams need to align on the session package, handoff timing, and what artifacts each team will produce in the shared workspace. The agenda is to confirm what goes into the participant 'session packet,' what version of the architecture prompt is used in each condition, who prepares the whiteboard and exports, and what it means for a session to be marked 'ready' by Friday. The expected outcome is a shared belief that logistics and tooling are aligned for Monday's pilot sessions.

members.name: Nina Patel
members.expertise: Internal experiment tooling, collaborative whiteboard integration, session templates, and event logging for engineering research studies
members.background: Nina is a senior software engineer who previously supported developer productivity experiments and now owns the technical setup for behavioral studies run inside the company.
members.private_state: She wants to minimize last-minute template churn because the whiteboard and logging hooks are brittle once cloned across session rooms, and she is trying to keep the pilot setup simple enough to support with one engineer on call.
hidden_assumptions: The 'session packet' means the digital assets participants directly interact with in the workspace: the architecture prompt page, whiteboard template, and submission link, not facilitator-only instructions.
The 'v2 prompt' refers to the latest wording committed in the study-tooling repository yesterday, which only changed formatting and examples but is functionally the settled prompt.
A session marked 'ready' means the room template is cloned, links resolve, and a dry-run passes; facilitator briefing details can still be adjusted afterward.
Owning the whiteboard setup includes creating the board, preloading sticky-note areas, and exporting the board artifacts after the meeting because those actions are part of the platform workflow.

members.name: Owen Morales
members.expertise: Study scheduling, participant communications, facilitator runbooks, consent flow coordination, and cross-team study execution
members.background: Owen comes from UX research operations and has recently begun supporting software-engineering studies that involve more custom technical environments than his usual moderated sessions.
members.private_state: He wants a clean handoff to facilitators by end of week so he can lock calendars and avoid retraining moderators over the weekend, and he is quietly worried about inconsistent materials across conditions creating operational confusion.
hidden_assumptions: The 'session packet' means the full moderator-facing bundle for a session: participant instructions, timing cues, consent reminders, and the prompt materials together.
The 'v2 prompt' refers to the revised Google Doc circulated after the methodology review on Monday, whose wording change to the pre-meeting solo activity was approved unless someone objected.
A session marked 'ready' means facilitators have the final runbook and participant-facing materials frozen and sent, so no substantive changes happen afterward.
Owning the whiteboard setup means creating the initial board shell and permissions, while facilitators or coordinators handle exports as part of session wrap-up.

When people say the treatment group gets 'individual notes,' that includes a private worksheet collected before discussion, because that is how moderated studies usually preserve pre-discussion thinking.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to finalize and send the 'session packet' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina means the participant-facing technical assets in the workspace are finalized: prompt page, board template, and submission/export links.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Owen means the full operational bundle is finalized: facilitator runbook, participant instructions, timing guide, consent reminders, and prompt materials.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both roles regularly use 'session packet' as a shorthand in their own workstreams, and because each bundle overlaps on the prompt materials, the phrase sounds sufficiently shared to avoid clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that both conditions will run on 'v2 of the prompt.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina is referring to the repository's v2 whiteboard/prompt template updated yesterday with formatting cleanup and example card placement.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Owen is referring to the methodology-review Google Doc version from Monday that changed the wording of the treatment group's solo-work instructions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts are genuinely called v2 in different systems, both are recent, and the meeting is about coordination rather than content design, so neither expects the label itself to be ambiguous.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a session being 'ready'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having all pilot sessions 'ready by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina believes 'ready' means the technical rooms exist, permissions work, the logging fires correctly, and a dry run can be executed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Owen believes 'ready' means facilitators have frozen materials and can run the actual sessions without any post-Friday changes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'ready' is a common progress term that usually goes unexamined; each person assumes the other's readiness criteria naturally include their own domain's checklist.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of whiteboard ownership and individual notes flow
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Nina will 'set up the board' for treatment sessions so participants can do individual notes before the discussion.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina assumes this means creating one collaborative board per team with pre-labeled private corners for temporary solo ideation that remain visible in the same board and are exported with the final board.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Owen assumes this includes a separate private worksheet or pre-discussion capture step for each participant, collected before the group board begins, while board export afterward is a facilitator wrap-up task.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both imagine a reasonable implementation of 'individual notes' and 'set up the board,' and because they are discussing handoffs rather than study design principles, the boundary between board setup, private capture, and session wrap-up remains implicit.
